subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Planning and writing an informative essay; peer editing
outcomes: Plan an informative essay with paragraphs and topic sentences
Write a first draft using conjunctions for cohesion
Check a partner's draft with the editing checklist

tf.s: An informative essay usually has an introduction, three main body paragraphs and a conclusion.
When you check a partner's essay, you should check meaning and content first.
When peer editing, you should only look at spelling.
tf.why: You check meaning first, then the language questions.

tf.s: Your essay should have a suitable title.
tf.why: Right, a good title tells readers your topic.

tf.s: You should start writing your essay before making a plan.
tf.why: Planning first helps you organise your ideas.

tf.s: The second draft is written at home and handed in with the first draft.
tf.why: Correct, attach the first draft to the second.

tf.s: A first draft must be perfect with no mistakes.
tf.why: A draft is a first try that you improve later.

tf.s: The model essay in this lesson is about submarines.
tf.why: Yes, the model essay is called 'Submarines'.

tf.s: The conclusion is the first paragraph of the essay.
tf.why: The conclusion is the last paragraph; the introduction comes first.

boxes.q: How many paragraphs should the essay have?
boxes.why: Introduction, three body paragraphs and a conclusion.

boxes.q: What do you check first in a partner's essay?
boxes.why: Meaning comes first on the checklist.

boxes.q: What should you do before writing a draft?
What tool helps you check a partner's draft?
Where do you write the second draft?
Which word links ideas to show contrast?
Which word links ideas to show a result?

boxes.why: You improve a draft into a final piece.

boxes.q: What should the model essay help you notice?
boxes.why: The teacher highlights topic sentences and conjunctions.

hunt.q: Where the second draft is written

mcq.q: What is the correct order of writing steps in this lesson?
o: plan, first draft, peer editing, second draft
mcq.why: You plan, draft, get feedback, then rewrite.
Linking words help ideas flow as one whole.

mcq.q: What do you hand in with your second draft?
mcq.why: Attach the first draft so the teacher sees your progress.

mcq.q: What does the introduction of an informative essay do?
o: asks the reader to buy something
mcq.why: The introduction tells readers what the essay is about.

mcq.q: You are writing about trains. Which is the best topic sentence?
o: Trains are a safe and efficient form of transport.
mcq.why: It states a clear main idea.

mcq.q: Choose the best linking word: 'Trains are expensive to build. ___, they save money over time.'
mcq.why: However shows a contrast between the two ideas.

mcq.q: Your partner's essay has a good idea in every paragraph but some spelling mistakes. What feedback comes first?
o: comment on the meaning and ideas

mcq.q: Why is it helpful to discuss your plan with a partner?
o: they can suggest ideas and spot problems early
it means you don't need to write
they will write it for you
mcq.why: Feedback at the planning stage improves the essay.

mcq.q: Why do writers make a second draft?
o: to improve the essay using feedback
to make it exactly the same
because the first draft is lost
mcq.why: Feedback helps you fix and improve your writing.

mcq.q: Why does an essay need a suitable title?
o: it tells readers the topic at once
mcq.why: A clear title prepares the reader.
